title: S4: Build shadow capped trees and the bounded Worker lookup library
description:
Background: the monolithic removal object is O(n) per change; a secondary-index miss alone cannot prove completeness; the probabilistic fact manifest leaves Worker membership unbounded; full minting must detect omitted committed authority without rejecting a fresh request signature or rebuilding SQLite; existing valid facts can contain large bodies and deep authority; and replacing the legacy removal slot before backfill would resurrect deleted content.

Scope: build the uniquely represented B-treap codec for FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree; pin layout_seed; store bounded FactRecords over unchanged chunked raw facts; create reserved suppression/action slots; derive shadow exact CLEAR/ACTIVE suppression values and exact/ANY authority rows; preserve the authoritative legacy slot/globals and feature-gate Workers; place local certification outside root identity; publish the shadow tuple through one CAS; diff by oid; and build TargetRegistry, AuthorityImpactRegistry, LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint, and RevocationLiability support for S5.
design: S4 is storage shadow mode, not semantic cutover. Legacy slot/globals remain authoritative. FactTree contains bounded proof records and reserved ActionSlots; SuppTree has one exact SuppSlot per admitted sid; AuthorityTree serves bounded canonical providers and preserves empty keys as NO_PROVIDER. TargetRegistry and AuthorityImpactRegistry are service-side certification support, not Worker trees. Shadow certification reports deep legacy authority, computes conservative fixed-key revocation liability, and supports zero-provider MemberPrincipal receipts without enabling them before S5. Equal logical sets under one seed must yield byte-identical pages and roots.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection around B-treap builds and shadow CAS never drops legacy deletion state; S4 bounded grants remain disabled and distinct cert keys retain byte-identical roots. An existing oversized message keeps its fid through raw-fact chunks without changing its fid; deep legacy authority yields exact checkpoint input. Golden vectors build the same set forward, reverse, randomized, incremental, and bulk and prove identical pages. Every page, tree row, ActionRecord, root, proof, lookup, ordinary-insert, fixed-value-update, and 867-subrequest bound is executable. A maximum ExactSids spec remains out of line and its ActionSlot pointer fits 512 bytes. At most 7 proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt; only afterward does its receipt EvidenceRef produce the maximum 8-ref ActionRecord, and a self-digest cycle rejects. Exact SuppSlot hit and absence authenticate CLEAR/ACTIVE or fail closed on a missing reserved key; no prefix or removal-fid Worker index exists. Dropping suppression, action pointer/evidence, authority, TargetRegistry, AuthorityImpactRegistry, future escrow, service reserve, admit-cell byte reserve, either legacy map, migration-seal object/byte reserve, attempt reserve, certificate reserve, pending isolation, or liability prevents certification. Support stages complete bundles outside ordinary keys, validates TargetBinding, separates at most 8 evidence FactRecords, 13 total base logical records, one base tree path, 64 effects, and a fixed-point union of 64 transitive authority consequences, and retains terminal liability. Ordinary publication updates impact scopes and rejects consequence 65. Revocation caps at 129 fixed paths and 1,032 copied pages. Attempt fencing uses fixed scratch keys, live-generation gateway checks, definitive write-lease drain, and a pre-CAS next-certificate claim. Worker lookup never scans or rebuilds SQLite and I4 remains until S5. Full suite passes. Shadow certification reconstructs complete AuthorityCandidateRegistry values, rejects candidate 65 for one NeedKey, and selects fallback or NO_PROVIDER from at most 64 candidates without scanning FactTree. Across 64 affected NeedKeys a removal examines at most 4,096 refs. It also proves migration seed derivation is acyclic and separately charges TargetRegistry and AuthorityCandidateRegistry rows/bytes. Shadow certification accounts independently for LegacyIamAttestation objects/bytes and per-publisher served-cell/inclusion-witness rows/bytes, rejects an absent or undersized mandatory slot, and exercises maximum legal 80-byte keys in ActionRecord/tree capacity fixtures. Shadow vectors retain one unpublished fid in several publisher inventories and converge on the same lowest-origin row/digest in every enumeration order. Migration sizing includes normal ActionSlot(Sid) plus SuppSlot structural backfill for a legal quarantine-only target, not only LegacyMask Migration slots. Shadow whole-cutover capacity preflight derives a provider-signed LegacySourceCeiling, proves the complete first-root manifest fits both canonical occupancy and a disjoint CutoverCapacityEnvelope, and fails while S4 remains writable if either is short. It distinguishes the pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment from the post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding and never assigns a layout seed or exact namespace before the frozen snapshot. Shadow preflight persists content-hash-matching CapacityCeiling and LegacySourceCeiling objects and charges their rows/bytes. Before each retry it reruns whole-cutover sizing and pins a fresh bootstrap/fallback pair while the current S4 generation remains writable. Shadow certification rederives candidate scopes only from declared liveness guards and rejects closure-wide candidate masking. Whole-cutover preflight charges every generation-staged service row/byte, proves each bounded batch plus the constant-size final activation, and fails while S4 is writable if any dimension or operation cap is unavailable. Shadow vectors reconstruct canonical raw bytes, recompute body hash and envelope fid, retry a collected ABORTED pin at a higher epoch without ABA, and retain every STAGING/SEALED/ROOTED cutover pin set.
notes:
Receipt uniqueness remains service-exclusive. NeedKey includes budget_class. Initial registry and checkpoint construction may scan off request; Worker lookup may not. The codec is the protocol-pinned uniquely represented B-treap, not an insertion-history-dependent B+tree. Directly targetable ordinary facts create reserved suppression/action slots before publication; later removal only changes fixed values. Tests retain detached-signature exhaustion and service-envelope exhaustion, more than eight transitive authority descendants, and the 64-consequence boundary. AuthorityImpactRegistry remains monotonic and conservative over losing and fallback providers. Descendant revocation liabilities remain escrowed in v1 rather than being synchronously enumerated or released.
Review closure: fixed ActionSlots point to bounded immutable ActionRecords. Shadow/migration sizing includes the principal ActionSlot required by a zero-provider LEGACY_GLOBAL plus migration ActionSlots and SuppSlots for LegacyMask. PendingCapacityEnvelope is isolated from canonical metadata and content.
Review closure 2: shadow certification derives DevicePrincipal over all same-key device fids and future-provider escrow, recomputes canonical SuppSlot witnesses across overlapping actions, and fails if any committed action loses its owner slot. Physical/certificate accounting includes out-of-line FactRecords and raw-fact chunks as explicit control-envelope dimensions.
Review closure 3: shadow migration builds a byte-canonical frozen LegacyEntryMap with one row per old removal entry and one receipt/action per equivalent lowest-fid group. Certification traverses ActionRecord EvidenceRefs through FactRecord raw roots and accounts legacy map object/bytes.
S4 off-request derives PrincipalProviderRegistry from every FactRecord; certification requires exact correspondence before S5.
Review closure 4: shadow support builds and certifies the immutable paged LegacyUniverseMap and LegacyMigrationSeal input, charges their object/byte dimensions, distinguishes eight evidence records from thirteen total base records and one base tree mutation, and models certificate sidecar capacity/reclamation.
Review closure 5: shadow capacity accounts every full signed admit-cell value, plus a separately capped migration seal. Registered publisher attestations occupy paged LegacyUniverseMap rows so their count cannot inflate the 4 KiB seal.
Review closure 6: certifier compares receipt evidence_fids/proof_digest only to pre-receipt proof_refs, then separately requires ActionRecord evidence to equal those refs plus the exact receipt ref.
Review closure 7 adds the forward losing-candidate registry required to make AuthorityTree fallback bounded; its fixed-width LIVE/MASKED state and the reverse impact registry update atomically. Shadow vectors also ratchet layout-independent cutover seed derivation and target/candidate registry byte capacity.
Shadow vectors include two proof closures for one provider, require AuthorityTree to bind the canonical provider plus closed-proof digest, and reject an arrival-order-derived candidate mask witness.
Review closure 8 requires shadow preflight to prove IAM retention and serving capacity, not treat either as a cache.
Review closure 9 adds deterministic multi-origin universe rows and sizes the previously missing normal owner-slot backfill.
Review closure 10 adds the masked-FactRecord/cutover cycle mutant and requires the shadow builder to order fenced old-source digest, legacy mask namespace, migrated FactRecords/logical rows, basis, seed, map root, then final cutover digest.
Review closure 11 requires an explicit layout_seed root field, aggregate proof-byte boundary vectors, and an O(1) PublisherCapacityCell publication check; nonpublishing deployments build their own direct witnesses off-request.
Review closure 12 splits the pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment from the post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding and adds a separately provisioned whole-corpus CutoverCapacityEnvelope/CutoverObjectManifest. Snapshot-derived seed and namespace values never appear before the drain; the normal PublicationAttempt pool never stages the first S5 root.
Review closure 13 adds retained capacity/source ceiling preimages and requires a fresh sized bootstrap/fallback pair before every retry fence.
Review closure 14 adds declared liveness guards to candidate/impact derivation and replaces a workspace-sized cutover transaction with bounded inert service-row batches plus one bounded activation.
Review closure 15 requires shadow certification to reject implicit nested-edge following and to derive Sid candidate state from effective_actions, including principal tombstones. Whole-cutover construction keeps root-free grandfather rows and generation-keyed certificate reservation inside the retained CutoverPayloadManifest, with the computed root bound only by the activation-tail CutoverCommitAnchor.
Review closure 16 Worker contract: after bounded closure validation, run the family-owned ephemeral gate with exactly one service-trusted now value; require canonical request shape, verb in request.VERBS, and exp >= trusted_now before grant_of. Legacy removal-global checks move to exact whole-closure SuppSlot evaluation, not out of the gate pipeline.
Review closure 17: the shadow build derives LegacyEffectCensus before hashing any migrated FactRecord and includes migration-only provider sids in authority candidates. The first S5 root retains the authenticated census closure and exact chunked reconciled-S4-root preimage. Worker reads claim one of 64 fixed WorkerReadLease slots and every tree/page fetch is root-and-certificate bound to that lease.
Review closure 18: shadow/cutover converts the complete frozen S4 effect set into a canonical S5-native LegacyEffectCensus while the old decoder is still present. LegacyMigrationSeal carries the admission-service LegacyTranslationAttestation; later S5 certification uses the S5 codec only and treats retained S4 bytes as a hash-checked audit preimage.
Review closure 19: shadow certification retains each provider binding across quarantine, verifies its FactRecord/raw root, and refuses to reclaim its count or capacity on restore.
Review closure 20: shadow mode builds and capacity-checks rooted proof preimages for distinct provider closures and seeds the S5 grow-only admitted-fact archive from both published and retained-quarantine legacy facts.
Review closure 21: shadow builders hash proof records before deriving candidate ids/ranks, produce distinct authority rows for distinct required-co-offer tuples, preclassify every legacy removal disposition from the frozen census/inventory, and size one proof-bound checkpoint per distinct over-budget candidate closure.
Review closure 21 supplement: migration sizing retains every paged legacy authority proof manifest/page without favorable deduplication and derives source candidate id only after the manifest oid. Shadow candidate values preserve exact co-offer match state.
Review closure 22: LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint refs use certified LEGACY_SOURCE_RANK(source proof depth, source fid, source candidate id), never the flattened checkpoint proof/provider, preserving mixed native/legacy winner order. Principal-provider, authority-candidate, and authority-impact registries store content-addressed bounded RegistryValueObjects behind 256-byte atomic pointers. NeedKey/co-offer and reverse-value bytes are capped. Every live target carries an AtomicCommitBudget; publication rejects before upload unless the complete 162-object/44,630,016-byte registry set, attempt manifest, and at-most-193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction fit. Mandatory mutations: checkpoint-reranks-legacy-candidate, inline-registry-values-overflow-atomic-commit, unbounded-authority-impact-value, and unbounded-required-cooffers.
Review closure 23: Worker suppression reads only the request fact selectors, the selected provider selectors, and that family edge’s declared AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS/FollowAuthority scopes; incidental proof support, unselected edges, and one-time authorization guards confer no liveness authority. BaseOfferNeedKeyRegistry and AuthorityBaseCandidateRegistry give symmetric bounded discovery: a new full NeedKey finds all retained providers, and a new provider updates every admitted full NeedKey for each exact/ANY base, recording COOFFERS_MATCH or COOFFERS_MISMATCH without a FactTree scan. Atomic publication now charges at most 162 registry value objects/44,630,016 bytes and a 193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction. Boundary fixtures use distinct target/evidence records and a 128-edge unique acyclic proof DAG. Required mutations: worker-suppresses-all-proof-evidence, provider-scans-or-omits-full-needkeys, and unclaimed-recovery-epic.
Review closure 24: authority proof admission is immutable once a CommittedAuthorityProof and post-commit AuthorityProofCommitProof bind the exact admission-basis proof; later canonical-winner changes do not re-resolve it, and only mandatory provider selectors plus declared AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS may mask it. Authority records separate bounded transport depth/cost from logical proof depth; NEED/REF descendants of a LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint propagate source depth with DERIVED_LEGACY_RANK. Ordinary raw facts use a separately sealed paged RawFactContentCommit in the isolated content envelope, so the fixed metadata PublicationAttempt carries one commit reference rather than every chunk. Required mutations: reresolve-admitted-proof-against-current-winner, checkpoint-descendant-uses-transport-depth, and inline-raw-fact-chunks-overflow-publication-attempt.
Review closure 25: AuthorityBaseCandidateRegistry is discovery-only and stores no full candidate id or winner rank; every exact full NeedKey derives its own candidate id/rank, including legacy checkpoint tie breakers. Each base candidate value enforces a 64-scope union in both provider-first and NeedKey-first order. Raw manifests bind chunk ordinals and byte ranges, RawFactContentCommit identity excludes upload generation, and a strong ContentCommitPin transitions PENDING to ROOTED with metadata CAS; only a fenced ABORTED pin is collectible, while cutover uses a paged pin set plus bounded anchor. A fact that both consumes and provides authority is budgeted for 162 registry objects/44,630,016 bytes and a 193-row/512-KiB pointer transaction including the pin transition. Required mutations: reuse-base-rank-for-full-needkey, late-needkey-multiplies-candidate-scopes, sort-raw-manifest-by-chunk-oid, content-generation-in-canonical-commit, and collect-sealed-content-before-metadata-cas.
Review closure 26: raw_root_oid authenticates the complete canonical fact bytes, while the running codec recomputes body hash and envelope fid; raw JSON hash is never substituted for fid. Deterministic ContentCommitPins use monotonic epochs so a fenced/drained ABORTED attempt can become a higher-epoch PENDING retry before re-upload without ABA. Cutover content lifetime uses an explicit STAGING/SEALED/ROOTED/ABORTED generation row, paged set, and atomic root anchor. Ordinary publication budgets 13 structural inserts and 221 prospective pages. Required mutations: hash-raw-bytes-as-fid, aborted-content-pin-blocks-retry, and collect-sealed-cutover-generation.
Application policy closure (review-corrected): each directly deletable FactRecord roots its exact DeleteOffer/OwnerBinding, provider FactRecord, AuthorityProofRecord, committed-proof identity, post-commit proof and deterministic target-bound ActorBindingProof. It does not retain an ActorBasis or historical composite root, so equal statements stay byte-identical across retries and old roots remain collectible. DEVICE bindings root a target-key-signed DeviceOwnerConsent and exact invite proof; unsigned competing invites confer no ownership. Shadow migration requires that consent or a prior immutable owner binding, migrates checkpointable deep proofs, and leaves S4 writable for missing, ambiguous or beyond-ceiling evidence.
Independent review closure 27: S4 atomically records a capped LegacyActorAdmissionRecord with each newly published deletable target and issues its commit proof post-CAS. It is migration evidence and service-side capacity, never a Worker tree; preexisting targets without a record cannot have ownership inferred at cutover.
Independent review closure 28: before enabling actor shadow recording, physically provision S4ActorAdmissionCapacityEnvelope. Every eligible new deletable S4 target atomically debits capped LegacyActorAdmissionRecord bytes, a CommittedLegacyActorAdmission row, deterministic proof slot, maximum proof object bytes, and proof write lease in the successful target CAS; a losing CAS debits nothing, while missing evidence or capacity leaves legacy S4 publication valid but blocks S5. Post-CAS recovery fills the reserved deterministic proof. Canonical and cutover envelopes retain and stage all dimensions. Current S4 invited devices use only device-signed contextual S4_DEVICE_INVITE_ACCEPTANCE, preserving shadow behavior without granting reusable S5 consent.
Independent review closure 29: the actor record exists first in generation-fenced scratch. The successful target CAS atomically debits S4ActorAdmissionCapacityCell and creates the commit row plus RESERVED proof slot; a losing CAS leaves the cell unchanged and scratch is reclaimable only after fence/drain. A valid legacy target missing contextual evidence or shadow capacity still publishes on S4 but deterministically blocks S5. Shadow authority publication also captures historical CommittedAuthorityProof timing for every new authority producer.
Independent review closure 30: fenced LEGACY_SLOT and LEGACY_GLOBAL receipts use a non-callable GRANDFATHER(LegacyEffectAuthorizationRef) bound to the exact LegacyEffectCensus row and old source, so valid S4 cross-user deletions survive without being falsely labeled OWNER/ADMIN and LIVE_GUARDS can never choose it. Every first-publication or on-demand authority closure is separately committed and post-commit-proved before a LegacyActorAdmissionRecord may cite it, including a preexisting provider and an alternate closure; finite S4AuthorityProofCapacityCell accounting is idempotent and a losing proof CAS consumes nothing. LegacyActorAuthorityTransport preserves the record original authority ref while a distinct authenticated CHECKPOINT transport binds and replays its exact paged source proof/candidate into the new checkpoint provider; the future checkpoint identity never overwrites the S4 record.
Independent review closure 31: ActionAuthorization verification is action-scoped for LIVE_GUARDS and grandfather actions, outside the direct-target OwnerBinding branch, so terminal MemberPrincipal/DevicePrincipal and LEGACY_GLOBAL actions cannot bypass it. Proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt; the later receipt EvidenceRef only determines ActionRecord. S4AuthorityProofScratchSlot and S4ActorAdmissionScratchSlot precharge object/byte/write-lease capacity before upload, preserve disjoint scratch plus canonical coexistence after a winning CAS, and fence/drain every losing attempt before reuse. An actor closure above the native proof bound is committed and post-commit-proved before the target CAS as PAGED_S4(S4PagedAuthorityAdmissionRef) over the canonical LegacyAuthorityProofRecord; cutover reuses that exact source to construct CHECKPOINT transport instead of inventing migration evidence later.
Independent review closure 32: S4PagedAuthorityAdmissionRef retains the paged proof oid as well as its strong commit id, so certification and GC never scan for the sidecar. A pre-fence bounded authority proof keeps its immutable DirectRoot commitment/proof through cutover; only a never-committed closure may receive CutoverGeneration, and a second row at the deterministic id aborts. S4 actor/proof canonical balances are workspace-global, initialized once, and never refill across fallback generations; an abort drains and rebinds only the separately precharged scratch pool while preserving both canonical cells byte-for-byte. Fixed row/proof caps and retry ratchets cover all three failure modes.
Independent review closure 33: AuthorityProofCommitProof is deterministically addressed by authority_proof_commit_id and a committed row with a missing sidecar takes restart recovery, never a conflicting cutover rewrite. Each paged S4 proof has an atomically RESERVED/FILLED S4PagedAuthorityProofSlot; its ref retains the filled proof oid, and restart deterministically recovers the sidecar before any target or cutover may cite it. The workspace-global actor/proof capacity cells have deterministic ids, retained capped envelope preimages, explicit cell/slot row-and-byte charges, and scratch-only fallback handoff. Final independent review reported no actionable findings; 51 repository-layout tests and 346 non-network tests passed with one planned skip.

title: S1: Harden the removal-index door and recover poisoned ingress
description:
## Background
The removal index can permanently poison a workspace because malformed closure keys reach inconsistent parsers, published-slot decode sits outside its guard, and a failing ingress pile replays forever.

## Steps to Reproduce
Admit a fact with a negative or ambiguous timestamp key and a deletion whose removal closure references it; turn, restart, rebuild, and sync a peer. The index encode/decode disagreement prevents publication and the same pile retries indefinitely.

## Scope
Reject malformed address keys at admission, make published-slot decode fail closed, quarantine or retire poison without replay loops, surface sync failure state, and align all key parsers.
design: This repair is independent of the new suppression format and must not add compatibility decoding.
acceptance_criteria: Real hostile-input tests cover malformed, ambiguous and negative timestamp keys at local ingress and remote sync; restart and rebuild recover; an unrelated valid pile continues; status exposes the failure; mutation of each guard makes a named test fail; full suite passes. The fact-address door accepts only a non-boolean integer timestamp in 0..999999999999999 plus exactly 64 lowercase hex fid characters, yielding one 80-byte canonical key. Negative, boolean, 16-digit-positive, explicitly signed, whitespace-padded, uppercase and ambiguous-colon forms reject before Fact or index admission; boundary tests use FACT_TS_MAX.
notes:
Review closure 8 makes fact-key width a door invariant rather than assuming Python's minimum-width :015d formatter is a maximum.
Review closure 11 distinguishes the new strict key door from sealed legacy state: an existing out-of-range key is reported and causes writable S4 fallback or explicit re-anchor, never silent drop or rekey.

title: S2: Freeze suppression, authorization, receipt, and bounded-proof contracts
description:
## Decision

Every registered family declares NEVER or an exact SELF/Parent/Ancestor suppression policy, a DIRECT_TARGETS matrix, and separate named AUTHORIZATION_GUARDS. SELF expands only after fid integrity. New facts structurally create every required exact SuppSlot and the reserved ActionSlot for any directly targetable sid or principal. Removal admission only fills existing fixed-width values. The three request-time trees use one uniquely represented B-treap whose priority and iterated weight-leader layout are pinned by layout_seed. Admission uses a separately provisioned service-exclusive key and workspace.body.pk is forbidden. Each Worker-authorizable role declares a compositional worst-case ProofBudget.

## Rationale

Explicit type ownership distinguishes cascade parents from incidental references. Exact CLEAR and ACTIVE slots let a Worker answer by fid without scanning removal evidence. Preallocation makes an already-admitted target removable without future structural insertion. A second authoritative removal-fid tree would duplicate evidence without serving the Worker. Unique representation makes equal logical state converge to equal page bytes independent of insertion order.

## Alternatives Considered

A suppression tree ordered by (sid, removal_fid) requires a prefix query and can structurally split during a later revocation. A second tree ordered only by removal fid duplicates evidence and serves no Worker authorization query. Rebuilding SQLite from the full fact tree on each request is unbounded. A conventional B+tree is insertion-history-dependent; globally repacking it after each write is unbounded. Synchronously releasing descendant liabilities makes ancestor removal proportional to descendant count.

## Scope

Freeze the exhaustive family matrix; selector, guard, target, SuppSlot, ActionSlot, receipt, service-key, capacity-envelope, B-treap, NeedKey, proof-budget, and Worker lookup encodings. Land callable skeleton APIs plus realistic named contract and golden-vector tests before bodies.
design: No implementation body starts before this decision and its skeleton contracts land. One workspace-global admission/publication service serializes cap-compliant roots. FactTree ActionSlots point at immutable action evidence; SuppTree has exactly one preallocated CLEAR or ACTIVE value per sid; AuthorityTree retains keys with NO_PROVIDER. A local reverse removal-fid database is cache only. Fixed-key removal updates are distinct from bounded ordinary structural insertions.
acceptance_criteria: The family matrix covers every registered family with NEVER or exact SELF/Parent/Ancestor, DIRECT_TARGETS, independent AUTHORIZATION_GUARDS, and per-authority-offer AUTHORITY_LIVENESS_GUARDS. Hostile selector and target tests reject naked sids, wrong paths, inherited-selector direct actions, absent slots, and a founder admission key. Canonical shapes cover SuppSlot, fixed-oid ActionSlot, bounded out-of-line ActionRecord, pre-receipt proof_refs, post-receipt EvidenceRef, TargetBinding, ExactSids, MemberPrincipal, LegacyMask, LegacyUniverseMap, LegacyEntryMap, LegacyMigrationSeal, MigrationBootstrapCommitment, CapacityCeiling, LegacySourceCeiling, CutoverCapacityEnvelope, S5CutoverBinding, CutoverObjectManifest, CutoverServiceManifest, CutoverServiceGeneration, TargetRegistry, AuthorityImpactRegistry, LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint, BaseRevocationRecords, RevocationActionBundle, PublicationAttempt, AttemptWriteLease, CommittedAdmission, AdmissionCommitProof, CapacityEnvelope, PendingCapacityEnvelope, ContentCapacityEnvelope, and RevocationLiability. A maximum ExactSids ActionRecord with at most 7 proposal/support proof refs plus exactly one receipt ref fits 16 KiB while its ActionSlot fits 512 bytes. Golden construction vectors prove proposal/support proof refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt before the receipt EvidenceRef determines the ActionRecord; a self-digest cycle rejects. BaseRevocationRecords has at most 13 logical records and only one base tree path. Exact SuppSlot reads authenticate CLEAR and ACTIVE and fail closed on a miss. Golden vectors prove forward, reverse, randomized, incremental, and bulk construction yield byte-identical B-treap pages under one layout_seed. Every exact binding has unspent liability; the independent terminal reserve survives per-fid masking. Complete transitive authority impact is capped at 64. The post-commit signer accepts only durable stored rows and a failed-CAS orphan receipt never certifies. Effects and consequences are separate from base records; removal is at most 129 fixed-key paths and 1,032 page objects, while ordinary insertion is at most 13 keys times 17 pages (221 pages). Capacity encodings separately charge admit cell count/bytes, both legacy maps, one capped migration-seal object/bytes, retained bootstrap/final-binding objects, certificate objects/bytes/write leases including one pre-CAS next-root reservation, and leased-root retention/reclaim rules. The pre-fence source ceiling and whole-root cutover staging dimensions are disjoint from the later single-operation attempt reserve. Fresh exact and ANY NeedKey, compositional budgets, bounded FactRecord and chunked raw bytes, three isolated quotas, and per-fid screening are pinned; full suite remains green with only explicit body skips. Canonical shapes also cover cutover_basis_digest, AuthorityCandidateRef, and AuthorityCandidateRegistry. Golden dependency vectors order logical universe rows, basis digest, candidate seed, LegacyUniverseMap root, then final cutover_digest and reject the cyclic derivation. A NeedKey has at most 64 complete candidates, one action examines at most 4,096 refs, fallback never scans FactTree, and capacity encodings charge TargetRegistry plus AuthorityCandidateRegistry rows and bytes. Pin FACT_TS_MIN, FACT_TS_MAX, MAX_FACT_KEY_BYTES, MAX_LEGACY_IAM_ATTESTATION_BYTES, MAX_SERVED_CELL_BYTES and MAX_INCLUSION_WITNESS_BYTES. Specify and golden-test the retained LegacyIamAttestation object and the served-cell/inclusion-witness row-and-byte CapacityEnvelope dimensions; the maximum ExactSids ActionRecord uses only longest legal keys. Freeze LegacyUniverseRows so PUBLISHED wins and otherwise the lowest verified publisher id is the single bounded quarantine origin; conflicting fact/derived bytes abort. Freeze distinct normal Sid and LegacyMask Migration owner-slot shapes for grandfather backfill. Existing-workspace migration retains capped canonical CapacityCeiling and LegacySourceCeiling preimages by oid; after restart a certifier content-hash-verifies and decodes them, then compares the exact CapacityEnvelope componentwise against the ceiling vector rather than against a digest. Candidate sorted_action_scopes derive only from exact family-declared continuing liveness guards on canonical proof-DAG authority edges; incidental support and one-time admission guards never become ambient revocation policy. Capacity shapes charge canonical root/frontier/active-generation cells and the retained cutover generation descriptor, while CutoverCapacityEnvelope separately charges inert service-row staging and pins bounded batch and activation work. Raw-content contracts distinguish raw_root_oid from the running envelope fid, use monotonic ContentCommitPin epochs for post-ABORTED retry, declare the cutover pin-generation state machine, and cap ordinary structural publication at 13 paths and 221 pages. Canonical shapes and hostile vectors also cover LegacyActorAdmissionRecord, LegacyActorAdmissionCommitProof, ActorAdmissionEvidence, AdminSubject, AdminAuthorityRef, key-signed DevicePrincipal target eligibility, and rejection of current-state legacy owner reconstruction.
notes:
Offering a selector means the fact may be suppressed; it grants no direct action. V1 content exact actions select SELF, while user/device revocation uses authenticated family-declared MemberPrincipal or DevicePrincipal scopes; parent and ancestor selectors only propagate. AuthorityImpactRegistry is a monotonic conservative superset including losing and fallback provider closures; only authority_consequences(action) is the exact fixed-point change set. PublicationAttempt carries a never-reused generation and OPEN, SEALING, ABORTING, or COMMITTED_COPYING phase. Publishers have no metadata-write credential. A manifest-bound gateway writes only fixed scratch slots under durable AttemptWriteLease records. Sealing drains definite write outcomes and CAS charges canonical occupancy before authority-exclusive copies. Existing removal keys are fixed-value updates with MAX_TREE_PAGES_PER_VALUE_UPDATE equal to depth; ordinary B-treap inserts use the separate prospective cap. V1 never walks descendants to release liability. Ratchets retain the post-commit signer, failed-CAS orphan receipt, target-specific liabilities, and terminal reserve.
Review closure: never inline target_spec in a tree row. FactTree ActionSlot stores FILLED(action_record_oid); certification fetches the content-hash-matching ActionRecord off request. Pending staging uses fixed overwrite-only slots and durable leases under PendingCapacityEnvelope; a full pending pool cannot block direct admission.
Review closure 2: freeze DevicePrincipal beside MemberPrincipal, a unique typed-principal TargetRegistry row, deterministic witness(root,sid), and the rule that overlapping actions retain both ActionSlots while SuppSlot names one canonical witness. CapacityEnvelope includes fact_record_objects/bytes and raw_fact_chunk_objects/bytes; base liability charges bounded proposal/support/signature/receipt evidence, not only tree and ActionRecord bytes.
Principal actions carry PrincipalBinding(target_fact_key, kind, public_key); admission recomputes all three fields from the authenticated target FactRecord. LegacyGlobalBinding is the sole zero-provider, target-fact-free migration exception.
Review closure 3: freeze EvidenceRef(role, key, fid, fact_record_oid), FactRecord.raw_root_oid reachability, an eight-ref ActionRecord cap vector, and the root-bound immutable LegacyEntryMap encoding/canonicalization invariant.
Freeze PrincipalProviderRegistry[(workspace, typed_scope)] as a capped sorted fid set and its control-envelope row/byte dimensions.
Review closure 4 freezes distinct evidence, logical-record, and tree-path limits; the authenticated LegacyUniverseMap/LegacyMigrationSeal encodings; and first-class certificate reservation, retention, fencing, and reclamation dimensions.
Review closure 5 freezes MAX_ADMIT_CELL_BYTES=32 KiB and MAX_LEGACY_MIGRATION_SEAL_BYTES=4 KiB plus their object/byte envelope fields. Publisher inventory attestations are fixed-width LegacyUniverseMap rows so the seal remains bounded.
Review closure 6 freezes MAX_ADMISSION_PROOF_REFS=7 separately from MAX_ACTION_EVIDENCE_REFS=8 and the acyclic construction order proof refs -> receipt -> receipt ref -> ActionRecord.
Review closure 7 freezes the acyclic cutover-basis/seed/map-root construction, the complete bounded forward AuthorityCandidateRegistry paired with reverse AuthorityImpactRegistry, MAX_AUTHORITY_CANDIDATES_PER_NEED=64, MAX_AUTHORITY_CANDIDATE_REFS_PER_ACTION=4096, and TargetRegistry row/byte escrow.
Authority candidates are proof-closure identities, not only provider fids: candidate_id binds NeedKey, provider and proof_closure_digest. MASKED stores the deterministic minimum effective action witness, so equal logical state is arrival-order independent.
Review closure 8 adds the exact fact-key grammar, retained IAM evidence object, and mandatory serving metadata to the frozen contracts.

title: S3: Implement explicit suppression selectors and dependency-closed masking
description: Background: direct-only deletion leaves attachment chunks projected and makes live/rebuild state diverge. Scope: implement SELF/Parent/Ancestor resolution, named dependency and guard-source validation, family author helpers, exact hostile-wire admission, compositional ProofBudget validation for new state, migration reporting for sealed over-budget legacy providers, many-to-many local victim rows, one mask for live/rebuild/ingress, and dependency-closed file deletion while the legacy removal slot remains authoritative through S4.
design: A deletion targets an explicitly bound, family-approved offered key. Every exact proposal references the target fact and names the selector token; admission recomputes TargetBinding and rejects naked or inherited capabilities not in DIRECT_TARGETS. Direct and group removals enumerate local victims through the same supp table. Authorization guards are computed separately and are never offered by a NEVER fact. No read-time graph walk and no generic inheritance from all deps.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a file retracts descriptor and chunks live, rebuilt and cold-joined; deleted blobs are no longer demanded; SELF is non-circular; missing/extra/non-ancestor/NEVER selectors and guard substitutions reject; multi-parent diamonds deduplicate. Every exact removal recomputes its target ref, target-family DIRECT_TARGETS permission, selector token and sid; naked sids, wrong refs and inherited parent/member selectors used as direct device/content targets reject, while removing the ancestor by SELF still cascades. Selector and winner-independent role budgets hold for newly authored state; every current family derives bounded proof-only metadata; the 519-hop legacy chain is reported for S5 LegacyAuthorityCheckpoint rather than rejected before S4; oversized new Worker-authorizable proofs reject; the attachment-bearing suppression theorem passes without waiting for S5 receipts; full suite passes.
notes:
S3 enforces MAX_FACT_RECORD_BYTES and compositional proof caps for new Worker-authorizable facts. Oversized raw content retains the same fid and uses S4 chunks. Existing valid recursive authority remains available on S4 and is surfaced to the fenced S5 checkpoint migration.
Review closure 2: the family matrix adds PRINCIPAL_TARGETS. Device revoke derives DevicePrincipal(pk) from an authenticated target FactRecord and masks every matching current/future provider; a naked pk or exact SELF-selector shortcut is rejected, while the authenticated self-bound device FactRecord may be the capability target. Duplicate valid device facts with distinct labels/timestamps are the required regression.
Review closure 11 caps family-declared terminal scopes per fact and makes a later membership+device provider consult both committed typed tombstones before choosing one canonical SuppSlot witness.
Application policy closure (review-corrected): the exhaustive family matrix declares DELETE_OWNER or NEVER and normalizes each directly deletable target to DeleteOffer(content.delete, SELF, OwnerBinding). A bare device_invite is membership/grant evidence, never ownership consent; only a durable target-key-signed DeviceOwnerConsent exposes a DEVICE actor edge. Actor classification checks for any admitted shape-valid direct-member claimant, including masked claimants, before considering a consented device edge. OWNER and ADMIN remain separate conjunctive proposal modes; NEVER and families without a matching DIRECT_TARGETS row emit no delete offer.
Independent review closure 27: the target matrix says a bare device_invite is never a DevicePrincipal target. Only the target-key-signed self-bound device row or DeviceOwnerConsent creates that action; once legitimate, the key-wide action still masks every invite/provider for the key.
Independent review closure 28: device_invite offers exact SELF to device.grant.delete so its retained owner or any live admin can retract that one provider without the invited key. This is distinct from DevicePrincipal: it neither expands to same-key providers nor pre-tombstones the key.

title: Post-cutover recovery: explicit suppression keys and indexed Worker reads
description:
## Background

The 2026-07-27 audit and design discussion supersede the previous open bead frontier. docs/TODO.md is the sole temporary implementation plan.

## Scope

Deliver explicit type-owned suppression offers and separate live authorization guards; immutable service-signed removal admissions; uniquely represented capped FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree B-treaps; exact preallocated SuppSlots and reserved ActionSlots; service-exclusive, capacity-checked atomic composite-root publication in an IAM-isolated metadata namespace; bounded Cloudflare Worker reads; poisoning recovery, product commands, ingress screening, regression coverage, performance repair, and documentation consolidation.

## Bankruptcy rule

Closed bead history is preserved, but every previously active bead is retired as superseded. No requirement survives unless docs/TODO.md restates it and a child of this epic owns it.
design: docs/TODO.md is authoritative. Facts explicitly offer SELF, Parent, and Ancestor suppression selectors or NEVER, independently of authorization guards. Workers exact-read one preallocated SuppSlot per selector; a certified CLEAR or ACTIVE value is sufficient and a missing slot fails closed. Actions fill reserved FactTree ActionSlots with one fixed-width ActionRecord oid; full target specs live in capped immutable ActionRecords. There is no second authoritative removal-fid tree; a reverse audit database is rebuildable cache only. All request-time trees use the anchor-pinned uniquely represented B-treap layout. S4 retains legacy authority in shadow mode. S5 cuts to the service-exclusive IAM namespace, preserves legacy effects without granting illegal current DIRECT_TARGETS authority, and certifies isolated control, pending, and content envelopes plus conservative RevocationLiability before bounded Worker reads.
acceptance_criteria: All children derived from docs/TODO.md complete with realistic tests. S4 preserves legacy deletions while shadow-building byte-canonical B-treaps and reserved suppression/action slots. Equal logical states under one layout_seed have byte-identical pages and roots in every construction order. A maximum ExactSids target spec, at most 7 pre-receipt proof refs, and exactly one post-receipt self ref fit a capped out-of-line ActionRecord while its fixed pointer fits one 512-byte ActionSlot; the proof digest authenticates the proposal/support refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization and never includes the receipt that it determines. BaseRevocationRecords is capped at 13 logical records but only one base tree path. S5 authenticates the frozen published-plus-quarantine legacy universe with root-bound LegacyUniverseMap and a separately capped LegacyMigrationSeal object, atomically enables commit-proof-derived ActionSlot and SuppSlot value updates, and removes legacy slot/globals only after revoking and draining legacy metadata writers. Every durable admit cell has both an object count and MAX_ADMIT_CELL_BYTES reserve for its full signed receipt; both migration maps and the seal have object/byte capacity. Illegal legacy direct-target pairs use victim-specific LegacyMask, and zero-provider globals precreate their principal ActionSlot. ExactSids and MemberPrincipal remain terminal and capacity-safe. AuthorityImpactRegistry caps the exact fixed-point transitive NeedKey consequence union at 64. PublicationAttempt uses monotonic generation fencing, fixed scratch slots, definitive write-lease drain, precharged canonical copies, and a pre-CAS next-certificate reservation. Certificates for current and leased roots are charged and reclaimed only after their last served-root lease or witness is fenced/released. Fixed-key revocation uses at most 129 changed paths and 1,032 page objects; ordinary insertion is separately capped at 13 times 17 pages. Descendant liabilities are not synchronously released. Pending and content quota exhaustion cannot consume control/revocation capacity, and direct admission bypasses a full optional pending pool. Workers use bounded exact reads without rebuild or per-hit evidence fetch. Malformed, cyclic, under-reserved, orphaned, unwritable, or uncertified state fails closed. Full black-box and mutation suites pass; README.md and DESIGN.md become the surviving records. Review closure 7: legacy migration derives layout_seed from layout-independent cutover_basis_digest before LegacyUniverseMap root and final cutover_digest. AuthorityCandidateRegistry caps each NeedKey at 64 candidates and each action at 4,096 pre-indexed refs, pairs atomically with AuthorityImpactRegistry, and forbids fallback scans. TargetRegistry and AuthorityCandidateRegistry both reserve row and byte capacity. Review closure 8: the migration fence revokes and definitively drains every legacy metadata writer before hashing the legacy universe; the first S5 root retains a capped, content-addressed LegacyIamAttestation with verifiable provider evidence. Fact addresses have an exact 80-byte canonical door with bounded 15-digit timestamps, and the maximum ActionRecord fixture uses that boundary. Every publisher preallocates row and byte capacity for its served cell and inclusion witness, and publication proves those slots plus the next witness before CAS. Review closure 9: LegacyUniverseMap chooses PUBLISHED or the lexicographically lowest verified publisher origin for a multiply retained fid, independent of inventory enumeration order. Fenced backfill precreates the normal Sid owner ActionSlot and SuppSlot for every legal grandfather target, including a quarantine-only victim; LegacyMask uses its distinct Migration owner only for illegal current target pairs. Review closure 12: existing-workspace cutover authenticates a provider-signed pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment that contains no snapshot-derived values, then a root-bound post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding. A physically disjoint CutoverCapacityEnvelope stages the complete first-root corpus; PublicationAttempt remains post-cutover and single-operation.
notes:
S5 is a coordinated workspace cut owned by the service-exclusive admission/publication authority. FactTree stores bounded FactRecords plus preallocated ActionSlots; SuppTree stores one exact CLEAR or ACTIVE SuppSlot per admitted suppression id; AuthorityTree retains fixed NeedKeys with NO_PROVIDER when empty. The key set plus pinned layout_seed uniquely determines B-treap pages. TargetRegistry and AuthorityImpactRegistry support certification and publication, never Worker reads. RevocationLiability reserves base records, up to 64 effect value updates, the fixed-point union of up to 64 authority consequences, path-copy pages, and durable service rows. V1 releases only directly named action liabilities and never enumerates descendants. CapacityEnvelope and ContentCapacityEnvelope are physically and IAM isolated. Publishers have no metadata-write credential; a generation-gated gateway writes only fixed scratch slots. AdmissionCommitProof is minted only after rereading committed cells. Worker reads remain 100 routed lookups and 867 cold-cache subrequests.
Review closure: ActionSlots contain only fixed ActionRecord oids; MAX_ACTION_RECORD_BYTES carries maximum target specs. PendingCapacityEnvelope is a third physically isolated quota. Fenced backfill precreates principal/migration slots, and a legacy normal selector is reused only when its exact current DIRECT_TARGETS pair is legal and resolves to the old victim.
Review closure 2: Device revocation is DevicePrincipal(public_key), a typed key-wide terminal tombstone covering every current and future device-provider fid; an exact SELF-selector shortcut is not the revoke action, although a key-signed self-bound device FactRecord can authenticate the DevicePrincipal target. SuppSlots contain one deterministic canonical witness, while every overlapping committed action keeps its own filled ActionSlot. CapacityEnvelope separately charges FactRecord and raw-fact-chunk objects/bytes for proposals, support, signatures, and receipts.
Review closure 3: ActionRecord roots a bounded EvidenceRef list through FactRecords to raw chunk trees, so sync/restart/GC cannot lose proposal, signature, support, or receipt evidence. The first S5 root also binds a frozen paged LegacyEntryMap: each old slot entry maps to one canonical lowest-fid action, while duplicate entries are evidence rather than impossible second receipts.
Implementation closure: PrincipalProviderRegistry is a capped exact service-side set of membership/device provider fids, maintained atomically with ordinary publication. Principal actions enumerate this set without a FactTree scan; Workers never read it.
Review closure 4: Separate MAX_ACTION_EVIDENCE_REFS=8, MAX_REVOCATION_BASE_RECORDS=13, and MAX_REVOCATION_BASE_TREE_PATHS=1; fixed-key publication is p+m+c <= 129 paths and 1,032 pages. Review closure 5: CapacityEnvelope charges admit_cells plus admit_cell_bytes for the complete retry receipt. LegacyMigrationSeal has its own bounded object/byte dimensions and fixed 4 KiB cap; the potentially unbounded registered-publisher attestations are individually capped rows in LegacyUniverseMap, not inline seal data.
Review closure 6: proof_refs contains at most seven proposal/support refs; those refs plus the service-derived ActionAuthorization determine proof_digest and the signed receipt. Only after the receipt fid and FactRecord/raw root exist does ActionRecord evidence append its one receipt EvidenceRef, for eight refs total. Review closure 8 closes the old-writer snapshot race, bare IAM-digest retention, mandatory serving-metadata quota, and unbounded fact-key findings.
Review closure 9 closes nondeterministic duplicate quarantine provenance and the absent normal owner-slot path for quarantine-only grandfather targets.
Review closure 10 breaks the LegacyMask content-hash cycle: the pre-record legacy_mask_namespace comes only from fenced legacy source state before any migrated FactRecord or LegacyUniverseRows digest, and LegacyMigrationSeal binds it beside the final cutover digest.
Review closure 11 adds the writable S4 abort generation, aggregate proof transport cap, complete multi-scope tombstone witness rule, explicit root-bound layout seed, and publisher-count-independent root publication.
Review closure 12 splits the pre-fence MigrationBootstrapCommitment from the post-snapshot S5CutoverBinding and adds a separately provisioned whole-corpus CutoverCapacityEnvelope/CutoverObjectManifest. Review closure 13 retains canonical capacity/source ceiling preimages for restart-safe comparison and provisions a distinct writable S4 successor before every retry fence.
Review closure 14 derives authority masks only from declared continuing liveness guards and activates a pre-staged service generation with a bounded root/frontier transaction.

title: S9: Complete adversarial, confluence, and mutation-proven coverage
description:
Background: the cutover suite lost 63 tests, leaves integrity branches uncovered, and its named suppression theorem is vacuous without attachments.

Scope: integrate S1-S8 under real daemons and sockets across cold join, partition/heal, proposal-before-admission, receipt-before-later-eviction, removal-before-victim, rebuild, authority shadow/restore, uniquely represented B-treap orders, exact CLEAR/ACTIVE slots, zero-provider migration, sealed deep-authority checkpointing, revocation and content/control reserve exhaustion, IAM cutover, fresh/committed authority lookup, malformed stores, and deterministic time; mutation-prove every contract.
design: Prefer product-level black-box tests; use unit tests for pure codecs, bounds, IAM adapters, and hostile branch pins. Equal logical state must yield byte-identical tree bytes. Request-time behavior uses exact SuppSlots only; removal evidence and reverse caches stay off the Worker path.
acceptance_criteria: Attachment-bearing live/rebuild/cold theorem and real daemon removal/auth lifecycles pass under partitions and hostile inputs. Failed-CAS receipts cannot replay, post-CAS copy/proof recovery precedes certification, and observed uncertified roots fail closed. ExactSids partial redundancy and target escalation reject; a successful B-only retry remains possible. Terminal eviction survives pre-masked, current-zero, future-provider, and opposite arrival orders. Capacity faults at detached signature, service record, full-size admit-cell bytes, reserved slot, registry, fixed scratch, write lease, either legacy map, migration-seal object/bytes, next-certificate reservation, retained certificate sidecar, and isolated content/control quotas cannot strand revocation. Delayed old writers cannot create arbitrary or canonical metadata keys; old tokens, read grants, and content credentials cannot address meta-s5. Transitive AuthorityImpactRegistry changes every fixed-point NeedKey; consequence 65 rejects the new provider. Forward, reverse, randomized, incremental, and bulk B-treap builds are byte-identical; priority, leader, padding, missing-slot, prefix-scan, removal-fid-index, insertion-history, eager-descendant-release, and shared-quota mutants fail. Zero-provider migration, sealed 519-hop checkpoint, provider 65, deterministic time, and exact 867-subrequest tests pass. Legacy-universe mutations drop a quarantine-only row, substitute its FactRecord/raw root, remove a registered-publisher attestation row, or trust a naked fid after restart and each fails certification. Migration-seal mutation omits its object/byte reserve or exceeds 4 KiB and fails before S5 CAS. Certificate-capacity mutation proves a missing next-root reserve blocks CAS, stale served-root fencing releases and deletes its sidecar, and a removal then publishes without borrowing escrow. Receipt-cycle mutation includes its receipt EvidenceRef in proof_digest and cannot construct a canonical receipt; named vectors pin 7 pre-receipt refs, then one receipt ref and an 8-ref ActionRecord. Evidence/base/path boundary tests pin 8, 13, 1, 129, and 1,032 independently. Every recorded mutation makes a named test red and the full suite passes repeatedly. Candidate-registry mutations drop a losing provider, revive a MASKED ref, choose a nonminimal fallback, exceed 64 candidates, or scan FactTree and each fails a named test; the 64-by-64 action stays at 4,096 refs. Cutover-cycle mutation derives layout_seed from a digest containing the seeded map root and fails. Target-row-byte and candidate-registry-byte capacity mutations fail before signing or publication. Legacy-fence tests delay an accepted old-prefix write across revocation and prove no snapshot/seal precedes definitive drain; post-fence writes reject. IAM mutations delete, redirect, oversize, alter prefixes, invalidate provider signatures, or GC the retained LegacyIamAttestation and each fails certification. Capacity mutations independently exhaust served-cell, inclusion-witness, PublisherCapacityCell, and certificate rows/bytes; registration or the publishing deployment fails before CAS, while a nonpublishing observer fails closed and repairs independently without blocking the canonical root. Fact-key mutations cover negative, boolean, 16-digit-positive, signed, whitespace, uppercase and ambiguous keys; the maximum 32-target/8-evidence ActionRecord uses exact 80-byte FACT_TS_MAX keys. Multi-origin quarantine tests enumerate identical signed inventories in opposite orders and require the same lowest origin, logical digest, seed and root; a first-seen-origin mutant fails. A legal legacy removal of a quarantine-only fact must create and fill its normal Sid ActionSlot/SuppSlot, while an omitted-slot or forced-LegacyMask mutant fails; conflicting same-fid bytes abort migration. Binding-order mutation pre-fence-final-binding assigns a seed or exact namespace before the drained snapshot and fails. Capacity mutation single-operation-cutover-scratch attempts to stage the first S5 root in the later one-operation pool and fails on a corpus larger than that pool; the whole-cutover fixture succeeds only with a complete, disjoint CutoverCapacityEnvelope and sealed CutoverObjectManifest. Capacity mutation digest-only-capacity-ceiling removes or GC-collects the canonical ceiling preimage and must fail after restart; redirected, oversized, and schema-mismatched ceiling/source objects likewise fail. Retry mutation reuse-active-fallback-on-retry attempts a second fence without a newly provisioned successor and fails while writable S4 remains authoritative. Mutation closure-wide-candidate-masking treats every proof-support fact as a continuing guard and fails paired grantee-only/grantor-only fixtures. Mutation workspace-sized-service-row-plan applies the full legacy service corpus in the final CAS and fails on a capacity-compliant corpus larger than one transaction; capped inert batches plus bounded pointer activation pass. Mutation cyclic-cutover-generation-manifest makes the service descriptor hash a manifest/root tail that already contains its oid and is rejected as an unconstructible content-hash cycle. Mutations hash-raw-bytes-as-fid, aborted-content-pin-blocks-retry, and collect-sealed-cutover-generation each make a named test fail.

Attempt injection delays an old put across OPEN to SEALING and ABORTING and proves unsettled leases block clear. Authority fixtures fill 64 and reject 65.
